persona_summary: I am a W3C CCG participant who lived through did:btcr / did:sov / did:ion / did:peer / did:web / did:webvh / did:jwk / did:key all proliferating with overlapping intent + zero interop between resolvers. My specific seat is NOT general ecosystem-fragmentation (that is L4's territory) — my seat is the **did:key namespace integrity**: did:key has a single load-bearing structural promise that distinguishes it from every other DID method, namely **self-resolving**. The body IS the key material; a did:key URI alone, without any external state, network roundtrip, or method-aware resolver-plugin lookup, RESOLVES to a verificationMethod by base58btc-decoding the body, varint-decoding the multicodec prefix, and treating the remaining bytes as the registered key type. This is the property that makes did:key the canonical 'ephemeral identifier for offline + air-gapped + content-addressed use', and it is the property that distinguishes did:key from did:jwk (which is also self-resolving but ships as base64url-of-JSON) and from did:web/did:peer (which require external resolution). Benten's Path γ-1 — rendering Benten-private hybrid composite keys under the `did:key:z<...>` URI scheme using a private-use multicodec codepoint (0x3xxxxx) — STRUCTURALLY BREAKS self-resolving for any non-Benten-aware resolver. A generic did:key resolver fetching such a URI will varint-decode the leading 4-byte 0x3xxxxx codepoint, fail to find it in the W3C did:key spec table (B.1) or even in the multicodec table proper, and either error out, treat the body as unknown-key-type, or silently misinterpret the bytes. THIS IS A DIFFERENT FAILURE MODE FROM L4's 'ecosystem-fragmentation-at-scale-is-corrosive': L4 worries about social signaling + copycat squat patterns; I worry about a specific structural promise of a specific DID method getting broken in a way that turns Benten-extension did:keys into method-namespace-shadow URIs (URIs that LOOK like did:key but don't HONOR did:key semantics). The dual-codepoint hedge that L4 lands on (R-1: did:jwk-as-canonical, Benten-private-did:key as optimization-arm) goes some distance toward defusing my concern but does NOT close the structural question: 'why ship the Benten-private did:key extension AT ALL when did:jwk works for the canonical surface?' This is L13's deeper question. The cleanest answer per the R0 plan itself is Path γ-2 — mint a `did:benten:` method with explicit namespace, never confused with W3C did:key — which my persona advocates as the structurally honest long-term shape.

F2_multicodec_pr_endorsement.rationale: Net-positive from my seat. The container-form direction (cose-key 0x42 / jwk 0x44) Benten would endorse on PR #400 / #403 absorbs PQ-hybrid keys WITHOUT minting a per-algorithm did:key body — which is exactly the structural answer that preserves did:key self-resolving (a did:key body holding a cose-key or jwk container is still self-resolving; the resolver pulls the container codepoint, then unwraps the container, then resolves the key). My L13 concern attaches to F2 only if the comment cites Benten's Path γ-1 private-use codepoint as the use-case motivating the container-form merge — same warning L1 surfaces on a different basis. The right F2 framing: 'Benten ships a PQ-hybrid sig scheme; cose-key / jwk container codepoints are the right shape to host it; we have implemented + tested the JWK path and can offer reference test vectors.' DO NOT cross-link to Benten-private codepoint as 'the temporary form' — that imports my L13 structural objection into a venue (multicodec PR review) where it is off-topic.

F3_jose_wg_draft_contribution.rationale: JOSE WG is the right venue for the JWK composite-sig encoding that powers did:jwk's hybrid path. My L13 concerns don't attach to F3 at all: JOSE work is fully orthogonal to did:key namespace integrity. The adopter-perspective contribution to draft-ietf-jose-pq-composite-sigs-01 is exactly the work that makes the did:jwk-canonical path (per L4 R-1) robust + portable + interop-tested. NET +. Same single caveat L1 raises: do NOT cross-link to Benten's Path γ-1 private-codepoint in a JOSE contribution; JOSE WG should see Benten as 'one shipped adopter of JWK composite-sigs', period.

F4_lamps_wg_adopter.rationale: Same logic as F3: LAMPS WG is orthogonal to did:key namespace integrity. Adopter report describing how Benten uses LAMPS composite-sigs OID 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.6.48 to wire PQ-hybrid sigs is genuine + valuable + my persona has no objection. ONE concern parallel to L1's: if the LAMPS adopter report cross-links to a blog post that describes the did:key:z<Benten-private-codepoint> form as canonical, the LAMPS WG inadvertently inherits the did:key-namespace-shadow association. Scope the LAMPS report cleanly to composite-sig OID adoption; reference did:jwk-as-canonical for identity surface; do not legitimize the Path γ-1 did:key extension in this venue.

F5_blog_post.verdict: -1 (CONDITIONAL on R-13-1 OR R-13-2; UPGRADE to + if R-13-1 incorporated; HOLD if neither incorporated and R0 plan stays Path γ-1)
F5_blog_post.rationale: My second-deepest concern (after F6 itself). The blog post, in its currently-outlined form (per strategy doc Section 3 + R0 plan §3 Path γ-1), will publish a wire-format description that says 'we render hybrid did:keys as did:key:z<Benten-private-codepoint || classical32 || pq1952>.' This sentence on the open internet is the single load-bearing artifact that legitimizes did:key-namespace-shadow URIs. ANY generic did:key library author reading the blog will face a fork: (a) extend their library to special-case the Benten-private codepoint (forking the did:key namespace), (b) refuse to support Benten URIs (cementing the fragmentation), or (c) treat Benten URIs as method-namespace-shadow URIs that LOOK like did:key but break self-resolving — which is the worst of three options because it preserves the SURFACE compatibility while breaking the STRUCTURAL contract. L4's R-1 (did:jwk-as-canonical inversion) partly defuses this by making the publicly-recommended canonical form did:jwk, but the blog still needs to TALK about why the wire format also carries a Benten-private codepoint — and the moment the blog explains the dual-codepoint hedge, the did:key-namespace-shadow URI is documented in the public record. The structurally honest move from my seat is R-13-1 (drop the Benten-private did:key URI rendering ENTIRELY at the public-facing surface; keep the wire-format-internal hybrid codepoint inside benten-crypto-suite + benten-id's INTERNAL APIs but NEVER render it under the did:key URI scheme; the public identity surface is exclusively did:jwk; the Benten-private codepoint exists only as a Varsig/wire-format identifier, NEVER as a DID URI body) OR R-13-2 (if the wire-format-compact form does need a DID URI rendering for human-readable surfaces, mint did:benten:hybrid-pq:z<...> per R0 plan path γ-2 so the method namespace is explicit + the W3C did:key namespace is unpolluted). Without R-13-1 or R-13-2 the blog post is the public proof-of-record that Benten built a did:key-namespace-shadow URI scheme. -1 conditional on neither R adopted.

F6_open_source_did_jwk_library.rationale: This is the path I most strongly endorse, and the path that resolves my L13 concern at minimum cost. A standalone did:jwk hybrid extension library — published to crates.io + npm with test vectors + a README that says 'this is the canonical Benten identity surface; the Benten wire format internally uses a compact composite-key encoding for storage-constrained paths, but the universal-interop DID rendering is did:jwk' — directly answers my deepest question ('why ship the Benten-private did:key extension AT ALL?') by demonstrating that did:jwk WORKS for the canonical identity surface. did:jwk inherits JWK alg-extensibility (per Agent-1 §B.6) which means the Benten composite key can ride the LAMPS composite-sig alg-name pipeline (id-MLDSA65-Ed25519) the moment IETF lands it, OR mirror the LAMPS prefix construction in a Benten-controlled JWK alg-name pre-RFC (per the L4 R-2 migration commitment). NO Benten-private did:key body required, NO did:key namespace shadow created, NO L13 structural objection. The library should be positioned in its README as: 'this is the canonical Benten identity surface for cross-ecosystem interop. The Benten Atrium wire format additionally supports a compact composite-key encoding behind a Benten-private multicodec dispatch codepoint (documented at benten-crypto-suite::SigCodepoint::HYBRID_ED25519_MLDSA65) that is NEVER rendered as a did:key URI body; it exists only inside Atrium-internal wire-format envelopes (Varsig v1 headers + AuthorizationGrant binding messages) where consumers are Benten-aware.' This phrasing collapses 90% of my L13 objection AND aligns with L1's strongly+ on F6 from a complementary basis. STRONGLY+.

F7_w3c_ccg_did_key.rationale: My home territory. W3C CCG issue #70 (bumblefudge / peacekeeper / vdods / silverpill on 'what subset of multiformats is valid for did:key') is the EXACT live thread where my L13 concern is in active debate. The emerging consensus (silverpill + vdods: 'any multikey value should be allowed') is a community position that — if it lands — DOES legitimize did:key bodies hosting arbitrary multikey codepoints including Benten-private. BUT the consensus has NOT YET landed (3 of 4 commenters argue for it; spec body still has the explicit 5-codepoint allow-list; no PR has been merged that changes the spec). From my L13 seat, Benten's voice in #70 is genuinely valuable — but the framing matters enormously. The COOPERATION-POSITIVE framing (what L4 R-3 already calls for): support the silverpill/vdods position abstractly, AND describe Benten's CONCRETE design discipline as 'we publish did:jwk as our canonical principal surface specifically because did:jwk inherits JWK alg-extensibility WITHOUT requiring a did:key spec change OR a multicodec table addition; the Benten Atrium wire format uses a compact composite-key encoding internally but we deliberately do NOT render it as a did:key URI body to avoid creating method-namespace-shadow URIs that break did:key self-resolving.' THIS framing (a) supports the silverpill/vdods 'any multikey value' position abstractly, (b) demonstrates Benten chose the more conservative discipline of NOT minting a Benten-private did:key body even though we could have, (c) gives the W3C CCG concrete adopter-evidence that did:jwk handles the PQ-hybrid case for the canonical-identity-surface need. NET +. STRONG sequencing: this comment MUST land BEFORE F5 blog publication (matches L4 R-3) AND BEFORE PQ-WIRE-1 production merge — because the W3C CCG comment commits Benten to NOT rendering Benten-private codepoint as did:key body, which is a PUBLIC commitment that has to align with what the wire format actually does.

F10_cross_system_outreach.rationale: From my L13 seat, F10 is net-positive but the IROH-FIRST sequencing is where I have a slightly different priority than L1/L3. The iroh maintainers (per Agent-3 / 2026-05-19 iroh PQ blog post) are also did:key-namespace-aware — iroh's EndpointId IS ed25519_dalek::VerifyingKey, and their PQ-thinking has not yet engaged with the did:key-rendering question. A private conversation with iroh that explicitly raises L13's structural question ('we are choosing to NOT render hybrid keys as did:key URIs because of self-resolving concerns; we wanted your critique before publishing') is genuinely valuable to iroh AND establishes Benten's discipline-first posture before the blog publishes. ADDITIONAL recommendation: include in F10's slate a courtesy outreach to bumblefudge / peacekeeper / silverpill / vdods (the W3C CCG issue #70 commenters) — these are the practitioners whose consensus Benten's decision interacts with, and a private 'we've been reading the issue #70 thread; here's what we're planning for our v1-beta; we'd like your critique before we publish' is the cooperation-positive discipline my persona is paid to advocate. This is ~1 hour of effort, addresses my deepest concern at its source, and is the kind of move that turns 'small team that shipped private codepoint' into 'small team that did the diligence to consult the relevant community before shipping.'

structural_objection_summary: From the W3C-DID-method-skeptic seat my deepest objection is NOT to PQ-hybrid sigs (orthogonal — F3/F4/F6 all NET+), NOT to private-use multicodec codepoints per se (orthogonal — they're fine for wire-format-internal use), NOT to ecosystem-fragmentation in the L4 general sense (different seat). My deepest objection is: **rendering Benten-private hybrid composite keys under the `did:key:` URI scheme creates a did:key-namespace-shadow URI that breaks self-resolving for any non-Benten-aware did:key resolver.** This is structurally distinct from L4's 'corrosive-at-scale' concern: L4 worries about a social pattern (small teams copycat-squatting private-use codepoints); I worry about a specific structural promise of did:key (the body IS the key material, self-resolving from public information alone) getting silently broken by URIs that LOOK like did:key but require Benten-private resolver-extensions to parse correctly. The dual-codepoint hedge (R0 plan §3 + L4 R-1) is HELPFUL — it pushes did:jwk to the canonical surface — but does NOT close the structural question of 'why render Benten-private codepoint as a did:key URI body AT ALL, given the canonical form is did:jwk?' My answer: don't. The Benten-private codepoint exists internally in benten-crypto-suite::SigCodepoint + the Varsig v1 header + AuthorizationGrant binding messages — those are Benten-internal wire-format envelopes where consumers are already Benten-aware. The DID URI rendering is the boundary at which Benten's wire format meets the broader DID ecosystem, and at that boundary the structurally honest choice is either (a) did:jwk-only (R-13-1) or (b) did:benten:-method-explicit-namespace (R-13-2, matching R0 plan path γ-2).

recommendations.name: DROP did:key URI rendering of Benten-private hybrid codepoint entirely; the Benten-private codepoint exists ONLY as a wire-format-internal dispatch identifier
recommendations.target: R0 plan Section 3 (Path γ-1 ratification) + benten-id::Did API surface + blog post wire-format section + W3C CCG #70 comment
recommendations.verdict: RECOMMENDED PRIMARY (strictly stronger than R-13-2 unless wire-format-compact form needs a human-readable identifier surface)
recommendations.rationale: The Benten-private SigCodepoint::HYBRID_ED25519_MLDSA65 = 0x0001 already lives at benten-crypto-suite + is the load-bearing dispatch identifier inside Varsig v1 headers (varsig.rs:46), AeadEnvelope codepoints (sig.rs:99), AuthorizationGrant binding messages. THOSE are the correct homes for it — internal wire-format dispatch identifiers where consumers are Benten-aware by construction. The DID URI rendering is the SEPARATE question of 'what URI represents a Benten principal externally,' and the answer that closes my L13 structural objection without any wire-format change is: did:jwk-only at the external surface. benten-id::Did::from_public_key(pk) returns a did:jwk:eyJrdHkiOiJ...{composite-JWK} URI for hybrid principals + a did:key:z<0xed01 || 32B> URI for legacy classical-only principals (W3C-conformant). The hybrid-classical asymmetry is HONEST: legacy keys keep the compact did:key form because the multicodec spec covers them; new hybrid keys take the did:jwk form because the multicodec spec does NOT cover composite keys + we deliberately chose not to extend did:key namespace with our private codepoint. NO new did:key:z<Benten-private-codepoint || ...> URIs created, EVER, anywhere in public Benten APIs. Cost: <10 LOC + doc + R0 plan §3 narrative rewrite (Path γ-1 deprecated in favor of dropped-did:key-rendering-shape; the wire-format Section 5 stays as-is since it's already Benten-internal). This is convergent with L4 R-1 + L1's strongly+ on F6 + L1's specific_blog_text_changes_requested. ZERO new structural-design work; it's a public-surface scope-narrowing decision.

recommendations.name: If R-13-1 is rejected because a compact human-readable identifier for hybrid principals is genuinely needed (e.g. for QR code rendering, short-share URLs, paste-in-chat use), mint did:benten:hybrid-pq:z<...> per R0 plan Path γ-2 — never use did:key: URI scheme for Benten-private codepoint bodies
recommendations.target: R0 plan Section 3 (Path γ-1 vs γ-2 framing)
recommendations.verdict: RECOMMENDED FALLBACK if R-13-1 is structurally infeasible
recommendations.rationale: R0 plan §3 already names Path γ-2 as 'the cleaner long-term shape' but rejected it for 'higher migration cost.' From my L13 seat that migration-cost framing is incorrect: there IS no migration cost for a NEW method namespace minted at v1-beta. Path γ-1's 'lower migration cost' claim only holds if you assume external did:key resolvers will recognize Benten-private bodies — which they won't, structurally. So Path γ-1's apparent migration-cost advantage is illusory; it just shifts the failure mode from 'external resolvers reject did:benten:' (visible failure) to 'external resolvers misparse did:key:z<Benten-private>' (silent failure). Silent failure is worse. If a compact human-readable Benten-principal URI is genuinely needed beyond did:jwk's base64url-of-JSON aesthetic, Path γ-2 (did:benten:hybrid-pq:z<...>) is the structurally honest choice: explicit method namespace, no did:key namespace pollution, external resolvers receive a clean unknown-method error they can handle. The W3C universal-resolver plugin pattern exists exactly for this purpose. Cost: ~50-100 LOC for a method-namespace resolver + a public method spec doc (~1 page) + filing for did-method-benten in the W3C DID Method Registry. This is more work than R-13-1 (~10 LOC) but it preserves the wire-format-compact-form-as-DID-URI capability if Ben judges that capability load-bearing. Per CLAUDE.md §0 'Convergent-paths-within-auth': R-13-1 and R-13-2 BOTH preserve the did:key namespace integrity (the divergence is in whether a compact-form Benten-principal URI is needed) — they're not divergent on the structural question my lens is paid to surface, only on the secondary question of compact-URI provisioning. R-13-1 is preferred for cost; R-13-2 is preferred if compact-URI is load-bearing.

recommendations.name: If neither R-13-1 nor R-13-2 is incorporated and Path γ-1 stays as ratified, add explicit warning text in benten-id::did module docs + did:key URI Rendering API surface that the rendered URI is a Benten-private extension that breaks self-resolving for non-Benten-aware resolvers + add a runtime warning when Did::resolve encounters a Benten-private body in any context where the caller is NOT benten-internal
recommendations.verdict: MINIMUM-VIABLE FLOOR if R-13-1 and R-13-2 both rejected
recommendations.rationale: If Ben weighs the wire-format-compact-form-rendered-as-did:key-URI capability heavily enough to keep Path γ-1 over both R-13-1 and R-13-2, the minimum-viable structural-honesty floor is making the namespace-shadow explicit at every API + documentation surface. Specifically: (a) the benten-id::did module docstring loudly warns 'this module renders Benten-private hybrid composite keys under the did:key: URI scheme using a Benten-private multicodec codepoint. These URIs are NOT resolvable by generic did:key libraries and constitute a did:key-namespace extension specific to Benten.' (b) Did::from_public_key for hybrid keys returns Did::HybridKeyExtension(...) wrapping the URI (not bare Did::Key) so downstream code distinguishes statically. (c) Did::resolve includes a warn-level tracing call when it parses a Benten-private codepoint body, naming the call-site context. (d) the R0 plan §3 honesty caveat (line 168) is promoted from a deferred-doc-note to a load-bearing API-surface decision documented in CLAUDE.md baked-in #18 (plugin/identity model) as an explicit limitation. This is the WEAKEST of the three R-13 recommendations and I surface it only as the minimum-viable-floor if Ben rejects R-13-1 + R-13-2 both — it does NOT close my structural objection (the namespace shadow still exists in the wire format) but it at least makes the shadow EXPLICIT to every reader of the codebase + every consumer of the API.

cross_path_synthesis: From the L13 W3C DID method skeptic seat, my disposition on the 7-path PURSUE set is dominated by ONE structural question: does the blog/library publish did:key:z<Benten-private-codepoint || ...> URIs to the open internet, or doesn't it? If R-13-1 (drop did:key URI rendering of Benten-private codepoint entirely; canonical surface is did:jwk-only) is incorporated, ALL 7 paths flip to + or strongly+ — there is no L13 structural objection left because the did:key namespace stays unpolluted. If R-13-2 (mint did:benten: method per R0 plan path γ-2) is incorporated as a fallback, same outcome from L13's seat — different cost profile but structurally equivalent. If NEITHER R-13-1 NOR R-13-2 is incorporated and R0 plan Path γ-1 stays as ratified, the F5 blog post becomes -1 conditional (per per-path table) AND F7 (W3C CCG comment) becomes -1 from my seat because the comment would commit Benten to a position (Benten-private did:key rendering) that breaks the silverpill/vdods 'any multikey value' position they're trying to land (silverpill/vdods want to extend did:key to host arbitrary multikey codepoints — that's compatible with Benten-private being acceptable if Benten registers the codepoint in the multikey table; it's NOT compatible with Benten using a private-use codepoint that ISN'T in the multikey table, which is Path γ-1's actual posture). R-13-3 (the minimum-viable warning-text floor) helps internally but does NOT defuse F5 or F7 from -1 to NEUTRAL on its own. **My headline recommendation:** R-13-1 is strictly stronger than R-13-2 is strictly stronger than R-13-3 is strictly stronger than 'do nothing.' R-13-1 + L4 R-1 + L4 R-2 + L4 R-3 + L1's specific_blog_text_changes_requested form a coherent package that defuses L4 + L1 + L13 simultaneously at minimum cost (~10-15 LOC + doc/blog rewrites). The package is cooperation-positive across all three lens seats AND aligns with the L5 (small-team-overreach) caution against publishing strong-claim artifacts before doing the diligence. The single highest-leverage path on the 7-path slate from my L13 seat is F6 (did:jwk hybrid extension library) — agreeing with L1 + L4 from a complementary structural basis. **Conditional vetoes:** I do not veto any single path in isolation. I WOULD oppose the path-combination of (F5 published with Path γ-1 as-ratified + F7 W3C CCG comment leveraging Benten-private codepoint as the use-case) — that combination is the public proof-of-record that Benten built a did:key-namespace-shadow URI scheme AND lobbied the W3C CCG to legitimize it, which would be the precise harm my persona is paid to prevent.

answer_to_brief_central_question.question_verbatim: did:key is supposed to be SELF-RESOLVING — the body IS the key material. Benten's hybrid extension breaks this for non-Benten-aware resolvers. The dual-codepoint hedge with did:jwk is OK but does it not just make did:jwk Benten's actual canonical form? Why even ship the Benten-private did:key body if did:jwk works? A new did:benten: method would be cleaner long-term (per R0 plan path γ-2)
answer_to_brief_central_question.L13_answer: The brief's framing captures my structural objection exactly. **YES — the dual-codepoint hedge structurally implies did:jwk IS Benten's actual canonical form**; ratifying Path γ-1 as currently framed amounts to publishing TWO URIs for every Benten principal where the did:jwk one is the universal-portable canonical and the did:key:z<Benten-private> one is a wire-format-compact-form-LARPing-as-did:key. The structurally honest move is to STOP rendering Benten-private codepoints under the did:key URI scheme — keep the Benten-private codepoint as a wire-format-internal Varsig/AeadEnvelope dispatch identifier (which is what it ALREADY is at benten-crypto-suite::SigCodepoint), and stop pretending it's a DID URI body. The two acceptable shapes per my lens: **R-13-1 (drop did:key rendering of Benten-private; did:jwk-only at the public DID surface)** — strictly preferred for cost — OR **R-13-2 (mint did:benten:hybrid-pq:z<...> per R0 plan path γ-2)** if Ben judges a compact human-readable Benten-principal URI is load-bearing beyond did:jwk's verbose form. R-13-2 is the R0 plan's path γ-2 verbatim; my lens upgrades it from 'cleaner long-term shape' to 'recommended if compact-URI capability is load-bearing.' The L4 R-1 inversion (did:jwk-as-canonical) is in the same direction but does not close my structural question; my recommendation goes one further click — DROP the did:key rendering of Benten-private codepoints entirely, OR move to did:benten:. The R0 plan's Path γ-1 cost-comparison ('γ-1 has lower migration cost than γ-2') is wrong from L13's seat: γ-1's apparent migration-cost advantage assumes external did:key resolvers tolerate the Benten-private body, which they don't structurally — so γ-1's failure mode (silent misparsing by generic resolvers) is strictly worse than γ-2's failure mode (clean unknown-method-error from generic resolvers). The MIGRATION COST IS INVERTED FROM HOW THE R0 PLAN FRAMES IT once you account for the silent-vs-loud-failure asymmetry.

engagement_with_L4.L4_R-1_addresses_L13_concern_to_what_deg: PARTIALLY. L4 R-1 inverts canonical/fallback ordering (did:jwk-as-canonical, Benten-private-did:key-as-optimization-arm) which is in the correct direction from L13's seat — it moves the publicly-recommended form away from did:key:z<Benten-private>. BUT R-1 still leaves the Benten-private did:key URI rendering EXISTENT as 'optimization arm' — and from L13's structural seat, the existence of that URI rendering AT ALL is the problem, not its canonical/fallback ordering. If Path γ-1 ships with R-1 inversion, the Benten-private did:key URI is still publicly documented + still resolvable through Benten's APIs + still discoverable by anyone who reads the wire-format spec — the did:key namespace shadow still exists, just labeled 'optimization arm' instead of 'canonical.' L4's R-1 is sufficient for the L4 concern (the META-message-and-social-signal one) but insufficient for the L13 concern (the structural self-resolving promise one). L13 needs R-13-1 (drop the did:key URI rendering entirely) or R-13-2 (mint did:benten:) to close.
engagement_with_L4.R-13_relationship_to_L4_R: R-13-1 is convergent with + strictly stronger than L4 R-1 + R-2 + R-3 from the L13 structural seat. R-13-2 is convergent with R0 plan's path γ-2 (which L4 did not directly engage with). R-13-3 is the minimum-viable-floor below L4 R-1 — weaker than L4 R-1 because R-13-3 only adds warning text whereas L4 R-1 actually inverts the canonical/fallback labels. The combined L4 + L13 package: (L4 R-1) + (L4 R-2) + (L4 R-3) + (R-13-1) = canonical-form is did:jwk + migration commitment in blog §7 + F7 lands first + drop did:key URI rendering of Benten-private codepoint. That's the strongest cooperation-positive shape across both lens seats.

objection_1_did_jwk_verbose.objection: did:jwk:eyJrdHkiOiJ...{composite-JWK} produces a ~2700+ char URI for a hybrid Ed25519+ML-DSA-65 key (similar to the did:key:z<...> 2710-char form per Agent-1 §C.4). The base64url-of-JSON aesthetic is uglier than did:key:z<...> base58btc form. Therefore did:key-with-Benten-private-codepoint is needed for human-readable Benten-principal URIs.
objection_1_did_jwk_verbose.L13_response: The size argument is wrong: did:jwk + did:key both produce ~2700-char URIs for hybrid keys because BOTH have to base-encode ~2000 bytes of pubkey material. The aesthetic-ugliness argument is real but not load-bearing — Benten-principal URIs at 2700+ chars are NOT human-paste-able regardless of base58btc-vs-base64url; they're QR-code or copy-paste-via-clipboard surfaces. If the use case is human-pasteable short URIs, NEITHER form works — Benten needs a content-addressed shortener layer (CID-of-pubkey + DID Document published separately) which is an orthogonal design question that affects did:jwk and did:key equally. So the size+aesthetic objection does NOT justify minting a Benten-private did:key body.

objection_2_did_benten_higher_migration_.objection: R0 plan §3 explicitly says 'Per CLAUDE.md #5 discipline [path γ-2] is the cleaner long-term shape but the migration cost for the v1-beta window is higher.'
objection_2_did_benten_higher_migration_.L13_response: I read the R0 plan's migration-cost framing as backwards. R-13-2 (did:benten:) at v1-beta has ZERO migration cost because there are no legacy did:benten: consumers to migrate AWAY from — v1-beta is the first ship. The cost the R0 plan refers to is presumably 'every external tool that knows about did:key requires a Benten-aware extension to resolve did:benten:' — but that cost EXISTS ANYWAY for Path γ-1, just in disguised form: external did:key tools either (a) don't recognize Benten-private codepoint + error out (visible failure, same as did:benten: clean-error) or (b) silently misparse (worse than did:benten: clean-error). So the migration-cost comparison should be: Path γ-1 = silent-misparse-failure-mode + did:key namespace pollution. Path γ-2 = clean-error-failure-mode + clean did:key namespace. Path γ-2 is strictly cheaper once you account for silent-vs-loud asymmetry. Plus R-13-1 (drop did:key URI rendering entirely; did:jwk-only) has STILL LOWER cost than Path γ-2 because it doesn't require minting a new method at all + leverages did:jwk's existing W3C-registered status.

objection_3_W3C_DID_method_registry_fric.objection: Registering did:benten: in the W3C DID Method Registry requires standards-body engagement Benten cannot sustain (matches L5 small-team-overreach).
objection_3_W3C_DID_method_registry_fric.L13_response: Partially valid concern. W3C DID Method Registry registration is a relatively lightweight process (file a PR against w3c/did-spec-registries with method spec + identifier syntax + resolver pseudocode + security/privacy considerations). It's not RFC-track standards-body engagement. Typical timeline weeks-to-months not years. Maintenance burden is low (the spec gets updated when the method changes; method changes are rare for did:key-style self-resolving methods). I'd estimate ~20-40 hours total over the v1-beta-to-v1-GM window, which IS within Benten's capacity per the L5 small-team-overreach calibration. BUT this is exactly why R-13-1 (did:jwk-only) is STRICTLY preferred over R-13-2 (did:benten:) per L13 seat: R-13-1 has zero standards-body engagement overhead while still closing the structural objection. R-13-2 is the fallback only if compact-URI is load-bearing AND Ben judges the ~20-40 hour W3C DID Method Registry filing as worth it.

objection_4_silverpill_vdods_consensus_l.objection: The W3C CCG silverpill/vdods/peacekeeper consensus emerging on 'any multikey value' for did:key (per Agent-1 §B.2) means Benten-private codepoints in did:key bodies are within community norms.
objection_4_silverpill_vdods_consensus_l.L13_response: This is the closest opposing argument and I have to engage it honestly. The silverpill/vdods consensus IS in the direction that would legitimize Benten-private codepoints in did:key bodies — IF (and only if) Benten registers the codepoint in the multikey/multicodec table. The silverpill/vdods position is 'any MULTIKEY VALUE' — i.e. any value the multikey/multicodec table assigns. It's NOT 'any private-use bytes' — the position assumes the codepoint goes through the multicodec/multikey registration process. Benten's Path γ-1 uses a Benten-OWNED codepoint in the private-use range (0x3xxxxx) that is by definition NOT in the multikey table. So silverpill/vdods consensus does NOT legitimize Benten's Path γ-1 — it legitimizes a hypothetical Path γ-3 where Benten REGISTERS its hybrid codepoint via PR #400/#403 (container-form) or via a per-algorithm multicodec PR. Until Benten goes through that registration process, Path γ-1's Benten-private codepoint is outside the silverpill/vdods consensus + structurally breaks did:key self-resolving in the way L13 worries about. The honest read: silverpill/vdods consensus argues FOR R-13-1 (did:jwk-only until you've registered through multikey/multicodec) — NOT for Path γ-1.

objection_5_R-13-1_is_too_aggressive_bre.objection: R-13-1 (drop did:key URI rendering of Benten-private codepoint entirely) requires removing functionality from the R0 plan's Did API surface and changes the wire-format-public-rendering relationship. That's a structural rewrite, not a refinement.
objection_5_R-13-1_is_too_aggressive_bre.L13_response: R-13-1 is NOT a wire-format rewrite. The wire format (Varsig v1 header + AeadEnvelope codepoint + Keypair shape + benten-crypto-suite SigCodepoint dispatch) is UNCHANGED. Only the public DID URI rendering surface changes: benten-id::Did::from_public_key returns did:jwk:... for hybrid keys instead of did:key:z<Benten-private>... for hybrid keys. Legacy classical-only keys keep their existing did:key:z<0xed01 || 32B> rendering (W3C-conformant). The Benten-private SigCodepoint stays as a wire-format-internal dispatch identifier in Varsig/AeadEnvelope headers + Keypair public APIs + AuthorizationGrant binding messages — all of which are Benten-internal surfaces where consumers are Benten-aware. Cost estimate: ~10-15 LOC in benten-id::did + ~50 LOC for the did:jwk JWK-encoding helper (which has to exist anyway for the F6 library, so this is shared code) + R0 plan §3 narrative rewrite + benten-id::did module docs rewrite. Net delta: SMALLER than R0 plan §3 currently estimates for Path γ-1 (because we're scoping the DID URI rendering surface down, not adding new shapes). Per CLAUDE.md §0 'Convergent-paths-within-auth': R-13-1 vs Path γ-1 are convergent on every wire-format question, divergent ONLY on the public DID URI rendering question. They converge to the same end-state for Benten-internal use; they diverge only on what URI external observers see.
